key_insight: VFIG leverages vision–language models to convert complex raster figures into semantically meaningful, editable SVGs, recovering both graphic primitives and textual/structural labels in a single pipeline.
problem_solved: Original vector source files for technical illustrations are often lost, leaving only flat raster images that are hard to scale or edit; manual reconstruction is slow, error-prone, and requires specialized skills.
method: Parse raster figures with a vision–language backbone to detect graphic primitives (lines, shapes, paths) and associated text/labels.
Map detected elements to a structured SVG representation (primitives + attributes + grouping) using a learned renderer/tokenizer and language grounding to preserve semantics.
Iterative refinement and layout-aware grouping to ensure geometric fidelity and editable, semantically annotated SVG output.
impact: Makes diagrams and technical figures immediately editable and resolution-independent, accelerating design workflows, dataset creation, and downstream diagram understanding tasks for AI/ML practitioners.
visual_elements: Before/after comparison: original raster figure vs. reconstructed editable SVG (side-by-side).
Pipeline diagram: raster input → vision–language parsing → primitive mapping → SVG output.
Primitive overlay: detected shapes and text boxes color-coded on the raster image to show element extraction.
Use-case icons/mini-chart: scalable export, semantic editing, and downstream diagram parsing improvements.
paper_title: VFIG: Vectorizing Complex Figures in SVG with Vision-Language Models
paper_authors: Qijia He, Xunmei Liu, Hammaad Memon, Ziang Li, Zixian Ma
